title: Ask for the tool, not the answer

job.text: Your manager asks: "What was West region revenue in Q3?" You paste the sales sheet into your AI.

naivePrompt: Here's my sales data. What was West region revenue in Q3?
basePrompt: Here's my sales data. What was West region revenue in Q3?

moves.label: Ask for a formula, not the number

text.plain: Don't calculate it yourself. Write a spreadsheet formula that adds up revenue where region is West and the date is in Q3.
text.tech: Don't calculate it yourself. Write a pandas script that filters region == 'West' and Q3 dates, then sums revenue.

text.plain: Run the formula on my file and give me the result it produces.
text.tech: Execute the script on sales.csv and report the value it outputs.

text.plain: Show me the formula so I can check it.
text.tech: Show me the code so I can review it.

text.plain: Please be very careful and double-check your math.
text.tech: Please be very careful and double-check your math.

text.plain: You are an expert data analyst.
text.tech: You are an expert data analyst.

rules.feedback: Same exact answer, 5 out of 5. The AI didn't get better at math — you asked it for a tool and had the tool do the math.
rules.lesson: The tool does the math; the AI only writes it.

output.showNote: Runs used two different formulas and got the identical number.

rules.claim: Applying this, the total is about 231,880.
rules.feedback: Half-way there. You got a formula, but the AI still guessed the total instead of running it. See "about 231,880"? Getting a formula isn't enough. Something has to run it: the AI's code tool, or your own spreadsheet.
rules.lesson: A tool nobody runs is still a guess.

rules.claim: West region revenue in Q3 was 251,330.00.
rules.feedback: Closer, but still guessing. "Be careful", "think step by step" and "you're an expert" change how the AI talks, not who does the math. It's still predicting the number. Which move takes the math out of its hands?
rules.lesson: Tricks change the voice, not the calculator.

rules.claim: West region revenue in Q3 was 312,904.10.
rules.feedback: Nothing changed. Asking the same question again just gives you another guess. Add a move that changes who does the math.

hints.nudge: Who does the adding up in your current ask? If the answer is "the AI", your rewrite needs to change that.
hints.gap: Spreadsheets add up 2,000 rows perfectly every time. The AI is good at writing formulas. What if you asked for the formula instead of the number?
hints.moves: Add Ask for a formula, not the number and Make it run the formula. Leave the politeness tricks out. They don't change who does the math.

whatYouDoDifferently.naive: "What was West Q3 revenue?" → 5 different wrong numbers, nothing to check.
whatYouDoDifferently.rewrite: "write a formula, run it, show it" → identical exact answer every run, and a formula you can reuse next quarter.

template.plain: Don't calculate this yourself. Write a spreadsheet formula that [what you need, e.g. adds up revenue where region is West in Q3]. Run it on my file and give me the result it produces. Show me the formula so I can check it.
template.tech: Don't compute this yourself. Write a script that [what you need]. Execute it on the attached file and report the value it outputs. Show me the code.

notes: ChatGPT: upload the file. It writes and runs code itself, so "run it" really happens.
Copilot in Excel: ask for the formula, then put it in a cell. Excel does the math.
A chat AI that can't run code: ask for the formula only, then paste it into your spreadsheet yourself. Never take its number.
